doc.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

title: Father's classical music, church playing and early piano lessons
summary: His father, a classically trained pianist who played in churches and taught, filled the house with classical music and offered lessons; Gordon took piano later and trombone at twelve.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. What turned you on to music? Was it the stuff in your household that was going on?

Pretty much. My father was a musician. And he studied classical music. He was never really into jazz. He came into jazz in the latter part of his life with the few successes that I had, that I was having, because he would be able to turn on the radio from a small town in Waynesboro, in Georgia, called Waynesboro, Georgia, and he could get the public radio station and they’d be playing jazz. And whenever they’d say my name on the radio he said that’s my son. So he started to listen to jazz. But he was a great lover of classical music. He loved Chopin, he loved, you know, Beethoven, Bach, Mozart and all of that. And when we were growing up we would hear that in the house. He had a reel to reel tape recorder that he kept on his piano and he wired speakers through the house in all the bedrooms and classical music was playing all the time. And then you know there was also the experience of going to church. Because he played in several churches in Waynesboro.

He was an organist, but he mainly played piano. Mainly played piano. And I remember him trying to get us to take piano at an early age. And it was really hard to sit at the piano for one-two-three, doing exercises and right outside of the window you could hear loud and clear the boys playing football and shooting marbles. It was like oh I don’t want to do this. And he didn’t make us do it, but we were offered to have music lessons because he also taught. But I took piano later on, I think when I was eleven I started playing trombone when I was twelve. And by the time I turned thirteen I got a chance to hear jazz for the first time on record. And that was a five record collection set of jazz, I think it was “Anthology of Jazz” put together by SONY or Columbia, whatever the record company was. And it belonged to a great aunt of mine that had just passed, and of the things bequeathed to the family was that. And it wound up at our house. She lived in Boston and we were in Georgia.
